the results are in line with a role for prenatal androgen exposure in the etiology of early-onset GIDs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEOAEs of children with GID are less influenced by the sex of rearing and more by their natal sex.
the CEOAE results are compatible with the idea that boys and girls with GID have a different prenatal androgen environment than control boys and girls.
CEOAEs are a promising marker of perinatal androgens and may be used to study the role of prenatal sex steroids in the development of GID in future studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sex difference in otoacoustic emissions may be used as retrospective marker of prenatal androgen exposure.
CEOAEs can be used as an objective marker of the androgen environment during perinatal life.
the use of CEOAEs as a biomarker of androgen exposure during early sexual development is a promising approach for future research on GID.
